records.title: [CI-ENGINEERING-CLOSURE-001] Recovered evidence, coordination and publication custody — Draft/HOLD
records.head: 911a3448e8e331cb097f1654bf861e20d77f57ca
records.body:
## Purpose and disposition

Closes the evidence-recovery and reusable-tooling scope of #706 / #761 with one reviewed **Draft/HOLD** candidate. Completed experiments were losing their original attempt/source distinctions, and publication helpers could reject valid unchanged libraries or attribute evidence to mutable input paths. This change preserves those distinctions and gives concurrent programme owners a bounded, read-only coordination tool.

**Resulting-source hosted qualification is pending.** Historical successes and local unit fixtures do not qualify this PR. No Ready transition, merge, auto-merge, runtime publication, active programme cancellation or new heavy campaign is requested or performed.

## Changes

- Add a GET-only/offline campaign summary with explicit run/attempt/source joins, required-job inventories, distinct skipped/failed/superseded states, optional ownership ledger, and incomplete-snapshot refusal. Sampled runner IDs are not a simultaneous account utilization count.
- Add an externally pinned publication custody verifier for actual binary bytes, canonical LFS pointers/local objects, changed provenance, source/build inputs, exact artifact/report/process/log joins, branch leases and publication-only children. It supports all four changed/unchanged Linux/Windows combinations. It grants no publication authority or semantic-test exemption.
- Pin the same captured bytes that are parsed/decoded; reject staged-index and branch movement. Preserve the existing real native, graphical, extracted-package and remote-LFS gates in the owner migration contract.
- Repair nullable tracked-delta ordering in the existing metrics helper without dropping or normalizing source identities.
- Add both new local unit suites to Documentation after its existing early runtime admission and before compilation; keep all existing steps and conditions.
- Change only Palette Windows `max-parallel: 2` to `3`. Linux stays two, GDExtension stays eight/eight, all cases/reducers/flags/timeouts/providers remain unchanged.

## Design choices and evidence

- **GDExtension:** reject exact #731 (mandatory policy failure); HOLD corrected #735 and #739 adoption. Corrected 16/16 ran 20m21s / 166.750 runner-minutes; final 14/18 ran 23m20s / 178.067. Their full PR cohorts took 33m22s / 280.20 runner-minutes and 33m27s / 294.35. Neither establishes an asymmetric benefit. The faster pre-repair 16/16 observation remains attached to its policy-red head. Keep 8/8; if later capacity admission justifies a change, 16/16 is the simpler qualified historical option.
- **Palette:** GO only for this Draft selection. The historical pair preserved six cohorts / 19 planned cases, reducing Windows span 351→208s and whole Palette workflow 450→358s, with 16.867→16.800 allocated runner-minutes. This is one measured pair, not a promised whole-CI saving. Rollback restores only Windows cap two.
- **RAM:** reject production adoption of both #732 staged-copy and #733 direct-checkout RAM-first. All 48 declared trials / 720 original process logs were recovered; all four RAM-first execution medians were slightly slower. Keep these negative research results, without merging their workflows.
- **Publication:** accepted main does not contain #762. The active owner retains its Draft publisher. The additive helper independently replayed original #762 evidence (42 Linux + 42 Windows + 18 extracted-Windows joins; 105 native and 1,283 build inputs), with a byte-identical independently reviewed receipt. The original #748 publication failure, its verifier-only recovery and later #762 campaign remain separate.
- **Capacity:** the owner's reported forty slots are not independently verified account entitlement. Historical cohort runner-minutes are planning references only; final GDE inventory is 657 cases versus historical 653, and this candidate keeps 8/8. No session-to-runner equivalence or saturation claim.

Generic helpers remain standalone until each publisher owner migrates and qualifies its own contract. This avoids editing active PUBPRES, Actor, ObjectShard, Equipment, Art, Batch Lab or SWARM campaigns. #729 and its source/artifacts/tests/reducer remain untouched.

## Verification and required next gate

Local integrated checks passed: **39 custody, 28 coordination, eight metrics, ten scheduling tests**, provider policy, all 93 workflow policies, pinned actionlint 1.7.12, 148-document / 33-question consistency, historical M11 integrity and pointer-only repository admission. The full custody command completed in 81.031s within its existing 300s allowance. Retrieval retained the prior Q19/Q32 misses; the new closure route ranks first. Independent specialists cross-reviewed source, original evidence and repaired negative controls.

The strict materialized admission is still pending (18 runtime files are pointers locally). New `tools/ci/*.py` files remain subject to Native/GDE/Palette source scope. Required resulting-source qualification comprises full materialized Documentation, all six Native families plus reducer, both GDE builds and all current 340 Linux / 317 Windows cases with graphical smoke and both coverage reducers, complete Palette GL/ANGLE cohorts plus reducer, and any additional final-diff gate. Conditional Draft skips do not count as qualification.

Existing local `gh` is unauthenticated; the approved connector has no new workflow-dispatch action, and the permitted browser fallback did not establish a usable route. This is a capability/authority blocker, not evidence of runner saturation. Before a separately authorized request: freeze the exact source/tree, refresh owners/queue/capacity, use the request ledger, and admit only the minimum full applicable cohort. Ready and merge remain owner decisions.

## Canonical packet and source binding

- [Decision packet](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/operations/ci-engineering-closure-001/FINAL-DECISION-PACKET.md) and [JSON](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/operations/ci-engineering-closure-001/FINAL-DECISION-PACKET.json).
- [Complete performance evidence](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/audits/2026-11-24-ci-engineering-closure/performance.md) and [machine-readable original records](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/audits/2026-11-24-ci-engineering-closure/performance.json).
- [Independent review](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/audits/2026-11-24-ci-engineering-closure/independent-review.md), [integrated validation](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/operations/ci-engineering-closure-001/local-validation.json), and [single request ledger](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/codex/ci-engineering-closure-001/docs/operations/ci-engineering-closure-001/CI_REQUEST_LEDGER.json).

Final remote head/tree and Draft check observations will be pinned in a follow-up comment after creation; the packet does not claim its own containing commit or convert an API PR head into a tested merge checkout. Accepted base: `00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f` / tree `06b62d73138028d1f7615b83edc9810491bf6287`.

records.title: Draft/HOLD: GIP-014 goblin real-game playtesting
records.head: 3e3aa217b49036ac4a87dd57073ad2cbb5a314c8
records.body:
## Purpose

Build the opt-in goblin developer playtester inside the real CyberSand Workbench. Policies propose bounded ordinary game actions; independent assertions inspect actual native receipts, material captures, actor input/ownership, authored history and isolated save/reopen results.

**Draft/HOLD. No Ready promotion, merge, production-default enablement or physical NVIDIA acceptance is requested.**

## Changes

- Dedicated Godot developer scene with Start/Pause/Stop, five disposable fixtures, six seeded personalities, current goal/action, observations and transcript export.
- Finite typed26-action adapter using existing Workbench controls and application-local input; fresh marked profiles protect owner saves.
- Native completion and independent readback assertions, preserving proposal/admission/refusal/partial/completion distinctions, pre-native cancellation and actual worker failure.
- Structured transcripts, exact source/runtime/fixture checks, semantic versus raw observation replay, and bounded real-game delta reduction.
- Existing test-framework integration, independent Python reader, and a focused hosted Windows/extracted-evaluator lane that uploads a runtime only after its required checks pass.

## Evidence and qualification

Accepted base: `00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f`. Published source: `5199cd5806e72819bbe512c000aee8dcee6efca1`; tree `45d04a51c6bd96fb8516b2f079902d440fa30308` matches the locally reviewed committed tree exactly.

Prior #749 remains separate at `a6fce059fa5620fcf4adb60cb9d2e7ed79050401`. Its successful run45066785091 is retained as reference-model evidence only; synthetic ticks are not native observations.

Development Linux evidence includes adapter005 (723 checks,49 records:46 completed/3 controlled cancelled refusals), controller-b002 (46 lifecycle checks), and a real CONTROL64 campaign (64 completed,17 features,381 assertion passes,1 not applicable). These retain their explicit pre-publication source snapshots. Current pure controls:113 GDScript assertion/transcript checks,151 policy checks,20 Python checks.

Final source-pinned matched personalities, longer campaigns, replay and Windows qualification are in progress. No naturally discovered ordinary gameplay defect is claimed from the passing development cases. Raw failures and environment interruptions remain in the evidence ledger.

## Scope and design choices

The goblin character is a visual tool-target/observed-pilot pointer with persistent policy goals. It can control an actual existing Kestrel through the normal game input path. No new physical actor model or alternative material simulation is introduced.

Reuse the retained source-matched native/Rapier libraries for this GDScript-only work, checking105 native and4 Rapier inputs, rather than claiming a fresh native build. Save/reopen asserts authored starting layout identity; evolved physical-state serialization remains unsupported.

Only goblin source, focused tests/tools/docs and its explicit branch-only qualification workflow change. Other active programmes and candidate branches are untouched.

## Guide

[Developer guide and consolidated qualification ledger](docs/research/gip014-goblin-gameplay-qa.md). Final evidence links and comparison results will be appended here after qualification.

records.title: [Draft/HOLD] ART-WORKBENCH-FINAL-001 — Art Workbench finisher
records.head: 2fc5974be7cd35aea6d5b1ad76d44d522e03bd17
records.body:
## Problem and scope

Art changes were split across provider, dialog, logging and timing candidates. This integrates them on accepted main `00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f` and repairs separately reproduced lifecycle and large-value processing defects.

**Owner correction:** LM Studio was not running during the original multi-second freeze. The primary protocol is an absent listener, Send, then Art's ordinary X. An HTTP 404 from a live mock does not reproduce it. Linux no-listener results and the separate accepted-socket teardown/CPU failures are identified individually.

**Draft/HOLD. No merge, Ready promotion or automatic merge.** Physical owner Windows/NVIDIA acceptance remains required.

Candidate source: `2fc5974be7cd35aea6d5b1ad76d44d522e03bd17`; tree `7e0505c5e675eec6e983ee474aca1e976075d802` exactly matches reviewed local checkpoint `b38b64b6f6a83be0a25be29605083f867f053719`. The initial integration `bbcb60bc` matches local `3532b8f8` at tree `44a12ffd80bd99aa8d6542698888475195b71b0c` and retains accepted main plus all four donor heads as parents. Publication uses the connected repository API because local Git push authentication is unavailable; complete local history and identity mappings remain in the evidence packet.

## Changes

- Preserve ordinary X as Hide and explicit Stop as cancellation; retain World-generation checks while hidden and fence reentrant audit callbacks before HTTP/native admission.
- Use nonblocking Godot HTTP polling, finite timeouts, bounded response allocation, disabled redirects and distinct transport/HTTP/malformed/capacity outcomes.
- Prepare large response/request values away from the UI thread, retaining one preparation task per provider, copied inputs, credential-snapshot validation and main-thread durable append/native ordering.
- Preserve complete admitted redacted session JSONL, bound live/error projections, reject malformed usage counters, and keep each new Workbench session independent.
- Bound Note/conversation geometry, keep Apply/Cancel reachable, populate large lists in frame slices, preserve stale-edit guards and correct scaled auxiliary windows. Messages over 4,096 characters use complete editable parts with direct part navigation; large clipboard input is paged before TextEdit shaping.
- Apply the exact #750 NVIDIA/LM Studio rosters, retain editable custom models/endpoints and historical configuration, and bind each Key dialog to the provider for which it opened.
- Add source-qualified Linux/Windows native and displayed regressions, a process-tree watchdog, and an isolated interactive Windows evaluator with an event-driven Ctrl+F12 timing checkpoint.

No native source rebuild or unrelated feature branch import is included. Existing donor branches are preserved.

## Design choices

| Choice | Reason and practical tradeoff | Alternative and reversal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nonblocking Godot HTTP polling with finite budgets | The controlled accepted-socket/no-header teardown exceeded 30 seconds under threaded HTTP; polling permits bounded Stop/teardown without a native rebuild. | Reintroducing threaded HTTP requires an independently qualified interruptible cancellation path. |
| One shared value-preparation worker; durable append stays on the main thread | Large JSON/redaction work can be cancelled without touching World/SceneTree from workers. Complete admitted receipts retain their ordering. Slow disks and native/display costs remain measurable limits. | A fully asynchronous journal requires a separate durability/ordering design. |
| 4,096-character editable parts for giant messages | Unicode shaping of a 64-Ki-character widget took more than four seconds. All content and edits are retained; moving between parts or pasting across parts resets local text Undo. Cancel discards the complete draft; native World Undo/Redo is unchanged. | Restoring a single giant widget should wait for a measured bounded text-layout implementation. |
| Keep accepted #727 session-only conversation behavior | Hide/reopen preserves collaboration within a game session; a new Workbench session starts an empty conversation and independent JSONL. Historical user files remain intact. | Automatic cross-session transcript restoration changes the accepted owner contract and needs a separate product decision. |

## Reconciled sources

| Record | Exact donor head |
| --- | --- |
| #756 | `8093a782a13a078ad6fa4fc9fdf11b969cbbf52f` |
| #763 | `2d63bba23932feb2c051c11df9d0775c24ea451d` |
| #765 | `cb88ab25d6dbdc8b459431d0189332bb7d37188a` |
| #766 | `48970266ae3b1ae47d2278d25ea312328078ddbd` |

#727's accepted session-only behavior is the baseline. #713, #744, #750, #559 and #558 were inspected alongside current PR identities, comments, ownership and CI; source-specific donor evidence is retained. #756 was actually non-Draft despite its title/body; this candidate is an actual Draft.

## Qualification and delivery

The focused Art workflow checks out this PR's exact head and uses official Godot 4.7 plus the unchanged source-qualified native/Rapier payloads. It exercises isolated headless and displayed Linux/Windows paths, real loopback conditions and native authoring, then tests the actual extracted Windows launcher and loaded module paths. No paid inference or private provider configuration is used.

Local qualification is source-specific: provider checkpoint `37a66929` passed 11,495 focused assertions; the integrated `d254751c` outgoing native group passed 122/122. Its interrupted broad matrix preserved 722 passing assertions across 37 completed cases and eight complete-body hash checks, but is explicitly incomplete. Fresh hosted processes are configured to cover network/no-server, incoming and outgoing CPU preparation, native lifecycle, near-limit changed Apply, and both actual process-exit directions with the unchanged two-second stall gate.

**Current exact-head focused run:** [45474493201](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45474493201) is in progress at `2fc5974b`. Final displayed, extracted-launcher and evaluator artifact results will be attached after qualification.

**Retained previous runs and corrections:**

- [45462474440](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45462474440), source `bbcb60bc`: the same obsolete long-note UI assertion failed on Linux and Windows; 265 other UI checks passed per platform. Its reviewed correction verifies the complete draft and joined parts separately from the bounded visible widget.
- [45463551930](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45463551930), source `9a130bc9`: all headless suites and all seven fresh-process matrix groups passed on both platforms (925 matrix assertions / 41 cases per platform). Independent reviews rehashed complete response bodies, changed-conversation content, clean source provenance and unchanged native payloads. The real edited 16,769,024-byte conversation applied in 311.257 ms on Linux and 344.189 ms on Windows. Actual process exits with unfinished preparation work were under 219 ms. This run still failed displayed UI qualification: four geometry assertions incorrectly compared a root-hosted popup with the smaller Art window, and Windows reached only 8,704/16,384 rows before a ten-second total-loading cutoff.
- The reviewed second correction requires actual transformed root/popup/footer containment, bounded monotonic row progress, every adjacent-frame gap including final deferred layout within two seconds, complete eventual 16,384-row loading and safe incomplete-state failure. The external 240-second UI-suite watchdog remains. It also retains an actual edited Conversation screenshot outside timed Apply intervals. Production behavior is unchanged; the only application-file change is a corrected sizing comment. New expected UI check counts are 268 headless / 272 displayed.

- [45469283511](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45469283511), source `eb0fb363`: displayed panel 272/272 and diagnostic input 18/18 passed on both platforms. All 16,384 list rows loaded with maximum adjacent-frame gaps of 138.352 ms Linux / 166.549 ms Windows; complete loading took 8.972 s / 19.205 s under software rendering. Linux passed native clipboard 69/69, displayed network 569 checks and incoming preparation 94 checks. Windows failed only two raw clipboard comparisons because its injected fixture bypassed the OS LF-to-CRLF conversion. Linux outgoing Stop missed its required unfinished-job precondition: real work finished in 38.464 ms before the next displayed frame; this was retained as failed qualification, not a responsiveness failure. Later displayed/package gates were unqualified.
- The current qualification-only follow-up compares both actual clipboard controls through the same OS boundary, retaining raw equality and stronger caret/selection/Paste/Undo checks (71 displayed). It reuses real near-cap context for enabled Stop before worker completion, adds an external POST-arrival oracle before body-size/path/JSON rejection, and retains all independent displayed outcomes before failing the stage. All frame, timeout, audit, cancellation and packaging gates remain. Independent reviews, exact Godot parsers, workflow-policy/Bash/YAML checks and Python-only negative POST-oracle probes pass; exact-head runtime remains pending.

Documentation/provenance also passed on source `eb0fb363` in [45469283449](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45469283449).

Documentation/provenance passed on source `9a130bc9` in [45463551803](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/45463551803); the current source is being checked separately. Earlier failed controls are retained, including the >30-second accepted-socket teardown watchdog, 2.488-second near-limit response pause and 3.329-second outgoing Send frame. External process terminations are retained without assigning an unproved cause. None of these proves the owner's physical Windows/NVIDIA no-listener freeze repaired.

The dated audit explains source reconciliation, review findings and evidence tiers: [Integration evidence](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/2fc5974be7cd35aea6d5b1ad76d44d522e03bd17/docs/audits/2026-11-24-art-workbench-final/README.md).
The evaluator guide includes the reproducible matrix and five-item owner checklist: [Owner evaluation](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/2fc5974be7cd35aea6d5b1ad76d44d522e03bd17/docs/operations/art-workbench-final-evaluation.md).

records.title: Draft/HOLD: AMBIENT-001 modular procedural actors and native perception
records.head: f4f94631d61d492554627949497e727b26043ccb
records.body:
## Draft / HOLD — opt-in AMBIENT-001

CyberSand actors currently expose human, scripted, external/local policy and passive control. This adds a reusable procedural ambient policy so ordinary authored Workbench worlds can acquire unscripted activity from their real local material environment.

**Disposition:** implementation checkpoint; remain Draft/HOLD. No merge, default promotion, native runtime publication, motor tuning or owner playfeel acceptance is requested.

### Working scope

- Pure-data, per-actor seeded engine with weighted steering and ordered temporary overrides, private module state, explicit simulation time, diagnostics and neutral fallback.
- Eleven implemented modules: wander, seek material, avoid material, avoid ledge, avoid boundary, escape obstruction, return home, rest, follow actor, avoid crowding and maintain altitude.
- Source-bound copied native material cache, bounded circular sampling, explicit stale/unavailable coverage, owner-issued ledge rays and copied compatible neighbors.
- Existing policy-v2 observations, actor/run/epoch/generation identities, leases and normalized commands preserved. Real ground/wheel and 4LY capability adapters; no direct World/Rapier mutation.
- Per-actor staged Behaviour profile editor, validation, native material picker, presets, runtime inspection, optional overlays and authored save/reopen.
- Six shared-module personalities and five genuine ordinary Workbench examples: Oil/Water garden, ledged walkway, industrial yard, eight-actor settlement and flight hall.
- Owner guide, module-authoring contract, focused regressions, matched native/Rapier comparisons and exact-source Windows qualification/evaluator tooling.

### Source and ownership

Based on accepted main `00cdb02f103265b6dc5224c68283e9a0c8cb449f`. #762 remains an unaccepted reference; capacity is the accepted **eight** logical actors. Shared changes are confined to the existing controller, observation, authoring and read-only sensor seams. Native material laws, the native World owner, Rapier bridge, physical motors, equipment and existing reactive/scripted policy implementations are unchanged.

Retained native source identity is `c53fd6f9d3d0f2b3f39396c7e605654f65c17299`; source-input hashes match the accepted Linux and Windows manifests. The Godot executable pins are the accepted official **4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f**.

### Evidence so far

Development runs exercised pure determinism, material relocation/aversion, real ledge geometry, actual simulation time, save/reopen, staged editor, normalized motion on Runner/Monowheel/4LY, ten-second retreat/pause, human handoff, all five native examples and the accepted population limit. Reduced native trajectory evidence and honest baseline comparisons are retained in `docs/research/ambient-001/evidence/`.

These are development-source results, **not a completed frozen-source release qualification**. An executor recovery erased temporary in-memory raw logs; the committed source and reduced evidence survived. Fresh source-bound process receipts are being generated. A first frozen import was killed under shared-host memory pressure and receives no successful-case credit.

The package/tooling has independent tamper, completion-marker, source/runtime identity and archive-integrity tests. The Windows workflow is deliberately gated by a branch-specific explicit request marker, so ordinary pushes do not queue an expensive campaign.

### Remaining gates

- Complete independently reviewed twenty-second same-rig personality comparison.
- Freeze the final code and run the focused actual Godot/native/Rapier campaign with original receipts.
- Actual Windows ANGLE examples/editor captures, portable package creation, pristine extraction, launch and save/reopen.
- Review final screenshots, measurements and package custody; update this description with exact tested commit and artifact links.
- Owner assessment of ambient believability and Windows/NVIDIA playfeel remains separate.

### Owner entry points

- [Workbench guide](docs/operations/ambient-workbench.md)
- [Module and perception contract](docs/systems/ambient-actors.md)
- [Mission ledger](docs/research/ambient-001/mission-ledger.md)

The intended walkthrough is: Actor Composition → choose an ordinary ambient example → Play → inspect an actor’s Behaviour profile → paint native Oil/Water nearby → observe its explanation and motion → customize a timer → Apply → save/reopen. Selecting or inspecting does not take control.
